title: Cenote Mul Tun - Sprouse 2016
credits: Cenote Mul Tun, Tulum, Quintana Roo, Mexico. Surveyed April 2, 2016 by Nathan Roser and Carol Vesely; map drafted by Juliana Rincón and Peter Sprouse. Length 180 m, depth 6 m. AMCS Activities Newsletter 39, p. 11 (2016). Source: AMCS Index to Cave Maps of Mexico (mexicancaves.org/maps/3684.pdf).
sistemaWhy: Mul Tun Spring (QRSS, 3084 m, explored from 2016-01 by Leal and Reato, connected to K'oox Baal in 2016-06) - the cenote, its cavern ring and the sump that leads on into that system. The other sistema, 'Cenote Mul Tun Siphon' (-KPZgftK2jzo0nw0kG41, QRSS, 109.7 m, 8.5 m deep, 2015-07, same divers), is the siphon beyond this map's sump: its 8.5 m depth is deeper than this map's 6 m and its 110 m isn't this map's 180 m. Neither sistema has a cave or a position in the database; which of the two the cenote belongs to (or whether the Siphon sistema is now part of Mul Tun Spring) is for the user to confirm.
unverified: No position at all: Cenote Mul Tun has no cave in the database (neither sistema Mul Tun Spring nor Cenote Mul Tun Siphon has a cave or a position), OpenStreetMap has no Mul Tun near Tulum (Nominatim: only Cenote Multun-Ha at Cobá, a different cenote 35 km inland; Overpass mirrors timed out), the web gives no coordinates (press reports of the 2016 photo trip: a 1.5 h walk through the jungle), and the map prints no coordinates, road or other cenote. The single control point is a NOMINAL anchor: the map's GPS-style mark (the circled cross by 'E') put on the K'oox Baal cenote of the database, the system Mul Tun Spring was connected to in 2016 (QRSS) - so the geometry is NOT on the ground, it lies over K'oox Baal. To fix: a field GPS of the cenote (the circled cross by 'E' looks like the survey's GPS mark). Scale and north are the map's own and trustworthy for a vector drawing (scale bar 0-50 m, 'Ngrid' = UTM grid north).
placementWhy: UNVERIFIED (see 'unverified'). The map is a vector PDF/SVG (Peter Sprouse / AMCS style): rasterised at 300 DPI (4.1667 px per PDF point, 2122 x 2573 px), then prepared (see 'prep'). Scale from the printed bar, 0-50 m between ticks at x 271.5 and 1140.5 (y 2306.5): 869 px = 50 m, 0.0575 m/px - the SVG's own tick coordinates (65.288 and 273.838 pt) give the same; the drawing's 75 x 85 m and the 180 m length agree. North: the arrow is 'Ngrid / Ncuadrícula' (grid north) pointing straight up: the drawing is aligned to the UTM grid, so 'up' in UTM (zone 16N) is exact. Position nominal.

prep.why: Vector map: the water is filled pale cyan (#dcffff), but the dry floor of the cavern ring between the water and the drip line (stipple and breakdown under the overhang) is left white, so the colour-fill trace would take the water only. Prepared in the scratchpad (scratchpad/multun/prep.py, not a repo script): the SVG rendered at 300 DPI with Chrome; the bold wall strokes (stroke-width 0.736 pt) rendered alone; the area inside the bold wall (flooded from outside over the wall and the cyan) minus the open-air area of the cenote (flooded from its centre over the ink grown by 16 px, so the drip line's ticks close it, then grown back; plus a disc of 48 px at (1035, 1172) for the rock in the open area) minus the water and the insides of the small bold loops (pillars) is tinted #dcffff on its white pixels; ink (stipple, boulders, ticks) is left as drawn.

trace.why: the prepared image's cyan (the drawn water plus the tinted dry cavern floor) is the passage: the outer bold line is the cave wall, the inner edge the drip line of the cenote's open-air collapse, the bold rings in the water (and the white-filled rocks) pillars and islands. Small map (0.0575 m/px): small thresholds and a 0.1 m simplification.

exclude.why: 'Amarre de línea de vida / Diveline tie' label

northWhy: 'Ngrid / Ncuadrícula': UTM grid north, straight up - exact in UTM coordinates

controlPoints.name: NOMINAL anchor: the circled cross by 'E' put on the database's K'oox Baal cenote - not a real position (see 'unverified')
controlPoints.why: nominal only, so the pipeline can run: K'oox Baal is the system Mul Tun Spring was connected to (QRSS, 2016-06); no position of Cenote Mul Tun is known

entrances.name: Cenote Mul Tun
entrances.knownEntranceWhy: the big hole - the open-air collapse ringed by the cavern - is the cenote entrance: the user, 2026-10-16 (its centre; the 'E' and circled cross at (1462, 1292) are on its east rim)
entrances.note: the map's only cenote (not in the database): its open-air collapse is the white centre ringed by the drip line; placed at the circled cross marked 'E' on the cavern floor east of the collapse (the survey's GPS/tie-in mark, it seems). The map writes no 'entrance' ('E' alone is ambiguous). Position NOMINAL - see 'unverified'.

symbols.why: The plan carries no depth numbers (only the title block's 6 m), no letter codes, no bones and no flow arrows (checked by eye at full size on the whole drawing; a vector map, so nothing is lost to the scan). The small black triangles and T-ticks in the water and on the cavern floor are drawn UIS detail (left as drawn, not typed). Kept by hand: the sump pointer, the low continuation, the named rock of the collapse and the diveline tie.

fix.why: a boulder's cloud outline read as a circled '2' (no circled numbers on this map)
